name: Load a part into a 6 in machine vise on parallels, clamp it and check it is seated

working.role: carries the part, cranks the vise, seats and checks

phases.what: Up and out of the table's way, then a slower final approach from above
Open wider than the part, the widest at about 74% of the reach
Close on the near and far faces; preload, then load, then lift 40 mm
Hold it up in front and turn it 28 deg to look at a face, then back
Carry it over the moving jaw, 20 mm clear
Set it on the parallels 6 mm short of the fixed jaw; let go by lifting off, not by opening into the jaws
The thumb pushes it along the parallels onto the fixed jaw, index and middle steadying the top
Crank the moving jaw onto the part until snug, about 2 turns a second: the fist keeps its orientation, the knob spins in it
phases.ends_on: 15 N of clamp: held, but it can still be pushed down

phases.what: Flat fingers press it down onto the parallels, a little toward the fixed jaw
The final pull on the crank
Press each parallel's exposed end and try to slide it: a seated part pinches them

sources.ref: Kurt Workholding, D688 AngLock vise: CAD and specifications (asset record d688)
sources.gives: the jaws, screw and handle the hand works

sources.ref: Kurt, 'Double Station Manual Vise Setup' (YouTube), measured locally with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker
sources.gives: reach durations, peak speed and aperture timing, crank speed (about 1-2 turns/s)

sources.ref: Jeannerod (1984) and Bhatia et al. (2022), reach-to-grasp kinematics, as used in trainual's accepted take
sources.gives: minimum-jerk reaches; grip aperture peaks wider than the part at about 70-77% of the reach

sources.ref: Johansson & Westling (1984), grip and load forces in lifting
sources.gives: the preload (0.23 s) and loading (0.21 s) phases before lift-off; grip force 1.7-2.2x the slip force

sources.ref: Machinists' vise setup as reviewed in trainual's accepted take
sources.gives: the order: set short, slide onto the fixed jaw, snug, seat, final pull, check the parallels

notes: The card behind the reference vise take (plan §5). Its numbers are the take's; generalising the take to any blank and parallel height is next.
